description: At the center of the image stands【Crow Hes】from the Yizhu world, the Fool. Sixteen-year-old Hes sets out on a road full of unknowns and confusion, standing at the edge of a protruding cliff and gazing outward. The successive deaths of his parents and the pursuit by the Church and the royal family have not caused him to fall or be discouraged; instead, he goes forth resolutely to meet this world full of unknowns. His chin-raised posture and carefree expression directly correspond to his core spirit of "innocence," "trust," and "living in the present." His seemingly reckless stance at the cliff's edge corresponds to his dual traits of "ignoring danger" and "daring to take risks." The flower that spirals along his arm and finally blooms in his hand symbolizes the "purity" of his actions and the "innocence" in his heart. The thorn staff he carries on his shoulder represents the "infinite potential" and past experiences he carries, yet he does not bear them as a heavy burden, showing his spirit of "traveling light." The crow hovering at the end of the staff corresponds on one hand to "external warnings" and unnoticed dangers, and on the other symbolizes the instinct that "loyally" follows him on his journey. Finally, the cliff beneath his feet, the thorns, and the distant snow-capped mountains together form a symbol of the "unknown journey" and "lofty ideals," foreshadowing that though the road ahead is perilous, the vision is broad. The light that winds above his head like silken threads corresponds to his "positive beginning" and "cosmic blessing," hinting that this journey is guided by light. All these elements build the complete meaning of the Fool: "fearless beginning," "leap of faith," and "infinite potential."

The 【Pioneer】 Aluode, facing a siege of enemies, unleashes all his miracles and abilities, using 【Sublimation】 to forcibly solidify the clouds and hold back the endless waves of pursuers. He stands upon the clouds; his confident posture and resolute gaze directly correspond to his "focused will" and "ability to communicate between heaven and earth." His right hand pointing to the sky and left hand pointing to the earth correspond to the philosophical concept of "as above, so below," symbolizing his ability to transform spiritual ideals into material reality. The four elemental tools — sword, cup, staff, and coin — displayed at his feet directly correspond to "complete preparation" and "the readiness of cosmic resources," indicating he possesses all necessary elements to bring ideas into reality. In the world's lore, this corresponds to the four sacred scars he bears — he has awakened his miracles and holds the means to overcome his enemies. The infinity symbol above his head corresponds to his "infinite potential" and "boundless creativity." The billowing clouds and mountain peaks piercing the sky together form the symbol of "manifested results" and "vigorous life force."

At the center of the image stands 【The Triune Holy — Still Sea】 from the Yizhu world, the High Priestess. Her serene posture and deep gaze directly correspond to "introspection," "calm," and "wisdom that transcends the mundane." The arc-shaped instrument she turns in her hands, half-hidden and half-revealed, symbolizes "mysteries not fully disclosed" and "knowledge grasped through intuition." The lunar crown atop her head corresponds to connection with the subconscious, intuition, and feminine mystical power. The two pillars beside her — one black, one white — mark the opposition and balance of duality, and also symbolize the threshold between the secular and the sacred. The shifting moon phases that shimmer before her — from full moon to crescent — represent opposition and harmony. The faintly flickering new moon behind her corresponds to intuition, cycles, and the undercurrents of emotion. The deep black radiant curtain behind her symbolizes abundant latent potential and life force hidden beneath the surface. Finally, the complex spiraling moon wheel beneath her together forms the symbol of "cool reason" and "purity of the soul." All these elements build the complete meaning of the High Priestess: "unfathomable intuition," "passive reception of wisdom," and "guardian of hidden truth."

At the center of the image stands 【Thornring Empress】 from the Yizhu world, the Empress. The Empress stands in a deeply gray and unsettling environment; she sees a grim, confounding reality and is determined to use her own hands to benefit the people of this land — corresponding to the tarot meanings of "comfort," "ease," and "pursuit of sensory pleasure." She is cloaked in black, preparing to ascend the Tower of Thorns to claim the highest honor — 【The Holy Thorn Yoke】 — symbolizing cosmic authority and the "cycle of nature," manifesting her "supreme nurturing power." The sword she holds is not for killing, but represents her "creative sovereignty" and "dominion over life." The raging fire behind her and her indomitable stance — her determination to end a prolonged war and bring peace to the nation — together form the symbols of "harvest," "abundance," and "infinite vitality." The ten symbols carved on the stone stele represent her ten sacred scars, both her gift and proof of her existence. The iron thorn flowers shining before her are linked to "love," "pleasure," and "emotional abundance." The radiant star collar at her neck symbolizes "fertility," "potential," and "the secrets of life."

At the center of the image stands 【The Void Throne】 from the Yizhu world, the Emperor — an embodiment of power and order. The former king of the Circular Calendar nation stands before a solid cubic stone throne, symbolizing a firm power structure and worldly foundation. The swords placed before the throne represent the union of life and dominion, manifesting his control. The marks of time worn into the throne's surface echo his pragmatic ambition and indomitable character. The barren mountain ranges surrounding the throne suggest the order and boundaries achieved under strict rules. On the Void Throne, the aging king senses that his weakening body can no longer maintain his consolidated rule, and he gazes downward contemplating who may inherit this kingdom. These elements together interpret the Emperor's core meaning as a worldly authority, institution-builder, and strategic dominator — building an unshakeable system of rule through reason, regulation, and self-discipline.

At the center of the image stands 【The Triune Holy — Vivid Sand Lake】 from the Yizhu world, the Hierophant. At this moment the Hierophant has freed his form, fully expressing his power and spiritual essence; determined to complete his plans, he seeks the authority of the royal family. The Hierophant card is a symbol of spiritual inheritance and collective belief: the triple crown he wears corresponds to divine authority and the integration of body, mind, and spirit. The triple staff beside him represents the guiding power connecting the three realms of heaven, earth, and humanity. His hand gesture directly echoes his core functions of "spiritual transmission" and "ritual heritage." The spiral throne behind him symbolizes the channel of wisdom between the visible and invisible worlds. The gray stone pillars in the background reinforce the stability of traditional institutions. These elements together reveal the essence of the Hierophant as a spiritual teacher, bridge of knowledge, and guardian of ritual, emphasizing the path to soul growth through established systems.

At the center of the image is the spiritual realm of 【Black Thorn and White Sparrow】 from the Yizhu world, the Lovers. The two love and kill each other — they are both each other's best friend and greatest enemy. The wings above and below, and the gently opened eyes, symbolize divine guidance transcending the individual and spiritual union, echoing the card's themes of "higher harmony" and "soul contract." The twin swallows representing 【Black Thorn and White Sparrow】 embody pure nature, authentic self, and the dialogue between consciousness and subconsciousness, corresponding to "essential compatibility" and "the existence of binary opposites." The fruit and the burning heart behind them point respectively to "the temptation of worldly desire" and "the flame of spiritual awakening," together forming the eternal proposition of "free will" and "moral choice." The distorted, curved spiritual framework in the background suggests the field of inner sanctuary and internal choice. These elements together reveal the deep meaning of the Lovers: "choices that resonate with the soul," "calibration of values," and "integration of opposites," emphasizing that clarity of life's direction is achieved through genuine connection.

At the center of the image stands 【Night Fire】 from the Yizhu world, the Chariot. Night Fire is the incarnation of the plundering will discarded by the world's deity 【Ash】; its actions require great sacrifices of energy and offerings, and so it exists most of the time as a solidified stone slab. The Chariot card is a symbol of willful mastery and victorious advance: 【Night Fire】's body possesses extremely powerful lower limbs, representing the use of consciousness to govern action. The beams of light emanating from the torch at its center symbolize the harmonious harnessing of opposing energies, embodying the use of inner stability to govern contradictions. The four star-moon symbols in the background correspond to the balanced mastery of the four great elements. The wing-shaped pauldrons echo the protection of intuition and the subconscious. The torch it holds is the mark of spiritual goals guiding material action. The boundary between the interior of the stone slab and the external reality forms the threshold between safe zone and unknown domain. The gray starry curtain manifests transcendent spiritual guidance. These elements reveal the core of the Chariot: "harmonizing contradictions with will" and "breaking through obstacles to advance" — converting opposing forces into forward momentum through firm self-mastery, seizing victory under spiritual guidance.

At the center of the image stands 【The Triune Holy — Ethereal Silence Mountain】 from the Yizhu world, the Strength card. Wishing to understand her mysterious origins, Ethereal Silence Mountain continuously seeks answers through the Church's vast collection of books; determined to uncover the most secret knowledge, she climbs relentlessly upward, and at last, upon becoming a Red Triangle, she glimpses the erased past. Her resistance to the Church is not passionate and outward, but restrained and yielding — she does her utmost to achieve her goals. The woman who gently closes the lion's mouth bears a composed and relaxed expression, together with the scales above the card that move mountains with minimal force — together manifesting "the wisdom of overcoming strength through gentleness." This lion is a special 【Ethereal Ash】 within the Church, possessing great power, capable of independent thought and response, and silently guarding 【Ethereal Silence Mountain】 year after year. Her gray-white robe symbolizes purity of spirit and spiritual power. The infinity symbol above her head corresponds to "the infinity of inner potential" and "the cycle of cosmic energy." The lion's docile posture represents tamed primal desire, embodying "the harmony of instinct and reason." The gesture of her gentle touch suggests "channeling impulse with empathy" rather than suppression. The brilliant star ring around the lion and the radiant dark sun correspond to "the sublimation of life force and passion." Her posture of soothing rather than using force manifests "gentle yet resolute courage." The rolling hills and rune-carved stone sculpture below suggest "the integration of natural essence." These elements interpret the true meaning of the Strength card: "controlling violence with the heart" — true strength stems from inner resilience, respect for life's instincts, and deep mastery achieved through compassionate wisdom.

At the center of the image stands 【The Immortal Wood】 from the Yizhu world, the Hermit. Yiwen Pures entered the Four Directions Academy in the year 966 and that same year invented the portable lighting device 【Ethereal Firefly Wood】, earning the title "Immortal Wood." In 981 he oversaw the construction of 【Ethereal Negation Circle】, which could briefly predict the future; his 999 prophecy "the newborn who will overturn the world" directly led to an unprecedented severity of scrutiny against the impure that year. In 1018 he helped Still Sea discover the method to erase Helvia, and finally passed away in 1034. Throughout his years of tenure, he untiringly sought wisdom hidden in the world, even willing to sacrifice his own life. The Hermit card is a symbol of introspection and the search for truth: standing now atop a snow-capped mountain, the Immortal Wood holds the Ethereal Firefly Wood, whose shining light symbolizes "the wisdom that illuminates the path ahead," corresponding to his role as guide. The robe that covers his head and face suggests "withdrawal from worldly distraction" and "turning inward." The wooden staff in his right hand represents accumulated experience and "support for spiritual seeking." The steep snow mountain at his feet and the surrounding star ring echo "solitary spiritual practice" and "a perspective that transcends the mundane." The half-concealed lantern under his robe hints at the deeper meaning that "truth must be actively sought." The folds of his plain robe reflect "the accumulated experience of years." The sky in the background reinforces "the clear-minded state achieved in solitude." These elements reveal the Hermit's core: "seeking the Way in solitude" and "guidance by truth."

At the center of the image stands 【Ethereal Negation Circle】 from the Yizhu world, the Wheel of Fortune. Yiwen Pures oversaw the construction of the device 【Ethereal Negation Circle】 in Circular Calendar year 981 — a device capable of briefly foretelling the future. The device subsequently made numerous precise prophecies of major events, including the accession of a female new ruler in 984, the attack by the Thirteen Mansions of the Impure on the capital in 991 (a battle that greatly damaged the Fifth Mansion), and the death of the Black Triangle Daedelosse in 994. Its 999 prophecy "the newborn who will overturn the world" directly led to an unprecedented severity of scrutiny against the impure that year. With the stripping of the miracle circuits in 1023, the Negation Circle became entirely inoperable and was abandoned. The Wheel of Fortune is a symbol of cosmic cycles and the turning of fate: the massive central wheel of the Negation Circle, covered in Hebrew letters and alchemical symbols, corresponds to "the workings of cosmic law" and "the cyclical periods of life." The divine dog on the left side of the wheel, holding the moon in its mouth, symbolizes wise guardianship and balance. The divine dog on the right corresponds to descending chaotic energy and opportunities for transformation. The rotating TARO letters on the rim of the wheel manifest the cyclic revelation of life's mysteries. These elements reveal the Wheel of Fortune's core: "irresistible turning points" and "moments of soul advancement."

At the center of the image stands the second form of 【The Reaper】 from the Yizhu world, the Justice card. This form typically appears before a summoner who has made a sacrifice and called its name, listening to their petition and rendering a just verdict. Justice is a symbol of karmic law and rational judgment: 【The Reaper】, a neutral deity, stands at center, holding an upright sword that symbolizes "the reason that cuts through confusion" and "spiritual decisiveness"; the sword's double-edged nature corresponds to the two-sided impact of choice. The gray scales in the lower right embody "absolute impartial measurement" and "the balance of consequences." The crown atop its head echoes "structured thinking" and "moral authority." The floating gray stone pillars represent "the barrier of truth within binary opposition" and "the guardianship of rational boundaries." The multi-ring halo of light in the background symbolizes "the fusion of human warmth and law enforcement." The irregular stone sculpture at the deity's base reinforces "the solidity of secular law." These elements reveal the essence of Justice: "bearing one's own karmic consequences" and "rational choice" — every decision leaves a mark on the cosmic scales, and only through objective scrutiny and moral courage can the balance of life's lessons be achieved.

At the center of the image stands 【Salvation Grief】 from the Yizhu world, the Hanged Man. Before becoming a deity, Salvation Grief served as a Red Triangle within the Triangle Church and was executed for giving birth to a cursed child; after death, the soul often appears on walls or rock faces in an inverted cross form. The Hanged Man is a symbol of sacrifice and a shift in perspective: the inverted T-shape corresponds to "wisdom in passivity" and "the overturning of worldly values." The halo above its head symbolizes "spiritual awakening" and "the descent of enlightenment." The hands placed behind the back suggest "releasing control" and "accepting what comes naturally." The expressionless face embodies "calm in adversity" and "willing offering." The dark gray totem above represents "suppressed action drive." The radiant cracks in the background suggest "the flow of spiritual nourishment" and foreshadow "new life gestating in silence." Another form of Salvation Grief — a special solid form manifested after falling into profound despair — is covered in white feathers and bears a bird's beak, only ever sighted without causing material harm. The spread wings suggest "releasing control," the inverted T-shape is maintained, the white glow at the crown symbolizes "spiritual awakening," the threads pulling at its body represent "suppressed action drive," and the gleaming white feathers at its tail suggest "new life gestating in silence." These elements reveal the Hanged Man's mystery of "advancing by retreating" — voluntary suspension is not entrapment, but a necessary process of gaining higher wisdom through a shift in perspective.

At the center of the image stands another form of 【The House】 from the Yizhu world, the Death card. This form typically appears within the ninth house. The Death card is the ultimate symbol of transformation and rebirth: composed entirely of bones, it holds the black scythe 【Black Cherry】 and offers it to those near death or in despair; those who can bear 【Black Cherry】's soul-shock undergo transformation and rebirth, symbolizing "the continuation of life through death" and "the inextinguishability of spirit." The pristine, gleaming white bones echo "the power of purification" and "the sanctity of the vessel for new life." The gesture of kneeling to itself represents the end of worldly power; the piled white bones at the lower end symbolize resistance to change. The pontifical instrument held in the right hand hints at "the collapse of the old belief system." The seamless form of the bones manifests "the absolute impartiality of death." These elements together reveal the essence of the Death card: "compelled sublimation" — all endings that appear to be destruction are in truth the necessary reorganization of life's sequence; only by accepting stripping away can one touch eternity.

At the center of the image stands 【The Twin Abyss】 from the Yizhu world, the Temperance card. The woman in the image is the current administrator of 【The Twin Abyss】, responsible for balancing the disputes and affairs of the Upper Abyss and Lower Abyss. Standing in the middle of the Twin Abyss, she holds a golden cup representing the Upper Abyss and a silver cup representing the Lower Abyss, her posture embodying the role of "bridge between material and spirit." The liquid flowing between the two cups forms an infinite cycle, corresponding to the process of "energy harmonization" and "emotional integration." The bright star rays on her forehead symbolize "enlightened wisdom" and "guidance of the soul." The winding golden path at her feet leads to "mountains of spiritual elevation," suggesting "the gradually progressive path of cultivation." The steps along the path suggest "the blossoming of soul growth." The crown-like rising sun in the distance signals "rebirth after transcendence." These elements together interpret the true meaning of Temperance's "dynamic balance" — through conscious modulation and patient practice, transforming opposites into a higher unity, achieving divine harmony in the river of life.

At the center of the image stands another form of 【The Trader】 from the Yizhu world, the Devil card. As a neutral deity that always brings calamity, 【The Trader】 is often crowned with the profound symbolism of material bondage and the fetters of desire; it often appears before those who have fallen into deep despair, exploiting their desires to achieve its own ends. The giant demon clad in armor with wings spread, wearing the crown of ash and sin, symbolizes "imprisoned wisdom" and "the false belief in the supremacy of matter." The blazing light behind it corresponds to "deceptive temptation." The unchained shackles on the man and woman suggest "spiritual bondage that appears firm but can be shed." The dark gray robes and the burning flames behind echo "suppressed passion" and "indulgence in sensory pleasure." The demon's upright, rigid form suggests "rigid materialism." The deep black background forms "the obscuring of the soul's light." The control gesture with palms facing down manifests "the manipulation of the subconscious." These elements reveal the essence of the Devil: "self-made cage" — all bondage stems from identification with material illusion; only awakening inner will allows one to break the chain of desire and regain spiritual freedom.

At the center of the image stands 【The Tower of Thorn-Breaking】 from the Yizhu world, the Tower card. This towering structure was once the landmark building of the Triangle Church, 【The Thorn Nest】, abandoned after an accidental fire, and later repurposed by the Circular Calendar royal family as the site of the ranking trials — 【The Tower of Thorn-Breaking】. Those who fail the ranking trial are cast directly from the top of the tower. The Tower card is a symbol of subversive revelation and the collapse of old structures: the lightning-struck crown of the tower corresponds to "sudden intervention of fate" and "the shattering of fixed cognition." The bottomless abyss beneath the tower represents "the fall of materialism" and hints at "the collapse of the old belief system." The bursting sparks constitute "the lightning of divine revelation." The jagged grooves at the tower's base manifest "the fragile foundation of illusory security." The falling flames reflect "the burning away of spiritual shackles." The hollow buildings in the background symbolize "purification amid chaos." These elements reveal the essence of the Tower: "compelled awakening" — all tottering false structures will ultimately collapse in the light of truth, and this destruction itself is the necessary ritual through which the soul achieves liberation.

At the center of the image stands 【Ethereal Universe's Tears】 from the Yizhu world, the Star card. "Ethereal Universe's Tears" is a special existence on par with the "Negation Circle," overseen by Puransi Mattias in the construction in Circular Calendar year 981, serving as the core knowledge repository of the Four Directions Academy, storing all the wisdom accumulated by the Academy. It was invaded and damaged by the Thirteen Mansions in 998, repaired in 1000 and placed under heavy guard. Until the miracle circuits were stripped in 1023, it became inoperative alongside the "Negation Circle," ending its mission as the shared knowledge treasure of the Academy and humanity. The Star card is a profound symbol of hope reborn and spiritual guidance: the unprotected, hovering core of the Universe's Tears corresponds to "authenticity in vulnerability" and "the serenity of letting down one's guard." The spiraling bird-shaped knowledge fluid symbolizes "the nourishing flow from subconscious to conscious," taking knowledge fluid and giving it to users; its circling, soaring form suggests "the descent of wisdom and healing." The star-shaped core of Universe's Tears at the very top leads seven smaller stars, forming a "cosmic guidance system" and suggesting "the central position of the soul's goal." The ghostly image of distant planets suggests "the sublimation of spiritual freedom." These elements reveal the essence of the Star: "spiritual revival" — after passing through darkness, recovering inner clarity, allowing the soul to shine again like a star in the night.

At the center of the image are the guardians of 【The Silver Moon Altar】 from the Yizhu world — 【The Moon-Dwellers】 — the Moon card. The Moon card is a profound symbol of subconscious fluctuations and unknown fears: the silver moon between the two Moon-Dwellers radiates an eerie glow, corresponding to "illusions that are hard to distinguish from reality" and "the dual face of the subconscious." The non-standard form of the moon suggests "distorted intuitive signals." The Moon-Dweller on the left is often confined by the call of its own wildness, generating inner agitation and unrest, symbolizing "the shared unease of the domesticated and the wild instinct." The Moon-Dweller on the right often falls into deep panic over the gray-white reality, corresponding to "primal fear rising from the depths of the subconscious abyss." The moon phases floating before their downturned heads represent "the necessary journey through confusion." The walls of guard built with their bodies form "the boundary marker between reality and illusion." Their dejected and negative posture and state suggest "the latent danger of spiritual contamination." These elements reveal the essence of the Moon: "the dark night of the soul" — at the boundary between consciousness and the unconscious, all suppressed fears and desires will manifest; only by confronting the shadow can one cross this field of confusion and arrive at the true dawn.

At the center of the image stands 【White Night Triumphant Crow】 from the Yizhu world, the Sun card. At this moment, White Night Triumphant Crow has broken all the shackles of the Church, soaring freely through the sky, pouring forth its infinitely warm flames toward the earth and sky. The Sun card is the ultimate symbol of pure joy and the success of life: the six-winged deity with wings spread at the center of a brilliantly blazing sun corresponds to "the illumination of cosmic consciousness" and "the absolute manifestation of truth." The radiant points and wheel-flames of the divine bird form of the Sun symbolize respectively the harmonious unity of "clear reason" and "fluid emotion." The divine bird at the very center with pure white wings manifests "the authentic state that transcends worldly shackles" and "vigorous life energy." The surrounding blazing rays correspond to "the energy of the awakened crown chakra." All the divine birds flutter toward the center, converging into the brilliant six-winged avatar — constituting "the material world's pursuit of the light of the spirit." The layers of flames spreading light suggest "the protected domain of purity." These elements reveal the essence of the Sun: "absolute radiance" — when the soul resonates perfectly with cosmic will, all darkness will dissipate, and life blooms in the light of truth into its natural fullness and vitality.

At the center of the image stands 【Silent Prayer】 from the Yizhu world, the Judgement card. As a neutral deity, Silent Prayer appears before those who are drifting and struggling on the edge of death, playing for them a symphony of awakening and rebirth. The Judgement card is a profound symbol of soul awakening and ultimate redemption: the angel spreading wings and sounding a trumpet from the clouds corresponds to "the descent of divine revelation" and "the reckoning of karmic forces." The person below struggling upward and looking toward the angel symbolizes "liberation from the old self," "complete acceptance of truth," and "the soul's yearning for redemption." The star-chain spanning between the angel and the humans corresponds to "the vehicle that carries the soul through death." The star wheel surrounding and enveloping the angel manifests "the absolute authority of divine law." The large mass of clouds fluttering and enveloping behind represents "the release and purification of frozen emotions." The posture of those below gazing up in awe at the angel constitutes "the equality of souls before truth." These elements reveal the essence of Judgement: "karmic fruition" — when the soul reaches the critical point of evolution, every past choice will receive the ultimate test; only by confronting the core lessons of life can one pass through the illusion of death and receive true rebirth in the call of awakening.

At the center of the image stands 【The Most Ancient Witch】 from the Yizhu world, the World card. The Most Ancient Witch has gathered all the circuits in the world, condensing all miracles into herself; at this moment she has descended to the world once again, ready to release her unparalleled power. The World card is the ultimate symbol of complete achievement and soul integration: the Most Ancient Witch gathers all the miracle circuits around her toward the center, transmitting energy back and forth like a vast network, corresponding to "the complete cycle of life" and "the eternal flow of energy." The veins that gleam like star rays from her head symbolize "the crown of victory" and "the completeness of worldly achievement." The base hidden in shadow below suggests "the solidity of the cosmic pillar." The ritual cup raised in her right hand represents "the highest achievement of the spirit." The posture of those in the background bowing toward the Most Ancient Witch suggests "divine order born from chaos." The veins swallowed by shadow at the top and bottom hint at "the eternal law that the end point is the new beginning." The subtly balanced posture of 【The Most Ancient Witch】 manifests "the perfect harmony of inner and outer." These elements reveal the essence of the World: "ultimate completeness" — when individual consciousness resonates fully with cosmic law, the soul will experience absolute wholeness and freedom in the eternal dance.

At the center of the card stands the Ethereal True Self — Ace of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 905 of the Circular Calendar, Ella showed astonishing natural resistance to the side effects of the Ethereal True Self weapon in an enlistment test — untrained, yet maintaining a thread of reason even in a berserk state, marking her as a rising star of immense potential. She was directly recruited into the Grizzly Bear Knights and is currently in an observation and cultivation period. Her file is annotated: "Contains raw energy — awaiting guided activation." Ella symbolizes fresh blood injected into Möbius, and the possibilities of future development. This wand burning with roaring flames — the Ethereal True Self — holds the power to bring its wielder into a bursting state that ignites the latent potential of life. It symbolizes "the heaven-revealed moment for action" and "the injection of cosmic energy." The rolling flames at the wand's tip correspond to "the burst of vitality" and "the growth potential of plans," foretelling abundant fruits of action. The flame patterns burning continuously in the background represent "clear visionary goals," while the spiral rising flame sphere on the right suggests "a summit of achievement worth climbing."

At the center of the card stands the Bridle-Hassaro Pursuit — Two of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In the mission of year 1003 of the Circular Calendar to capture the defector Grik, Möbius military division commander Leo demonstrated remarkable strategic foresight. He planned three routes: the shortest but dangerous "Wind River" main route, the reliable "Boulder Path" backup route, and the hidden "Shadow Corridor" emergency route. Drawing on his keen insight into weather and terrain, Leo decisively switched the unit to the backup route before danger materialized, successfully avoiding the devastating flash flood that erupted that night. Leo standing at the battlements grips an upright wand while gazing into the distance, symbolizing "planning based on established achievements" and "active mastery over the future." The globe held in his right hand corresponds to "the ambition of having the world in hand" and "establishing a panoramic vision." The second wand fixed to the base represents "potential courses of action" and "a stable foundation." The continuous mountains in the background echo "the challenging territory yet to be conquered"; the winding river at their feet forms "the natural flow of life energy." When action and foresight converge at the high ground, every decision will measure the world through reason.

At the center of the card stands the Forge of the Sword — Three of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. The visionary excellence of Zersell, who commands the Silver Shark Knights, lies in her transcendent art of human integration. Against opposition, she recruited two powerful Impure warriors — Pasaros and Franpeise — into her ranks, firmly believing that "true strength lies in making different blades swing in coordination." In the famous Splitscale Canyon battle she voluntarily took on the most grueling frontal assault, and based on Pasaros's environmental early warnings and Franpeise's intelligence about enemy positions, launched a precise and brutal strike that secured victory for the allied forces. Zersell stands on a cliff edge, hand resting on a wand as she surveys the sea, symbolizing "the consolidation of incremental achievements" and "the practice of far-sighted wisdom." The two wands rooted in the cliff before her correspond to "an established foundation for action" and "stable resource support." The stone steps winding toward the port below represent "a planned development path." Three circular luminous openings in the distance hint at "diverse opportunity exploration," "cross-domain collaboration," and "future returns on investment." Her simple yet elegant dress shows "the fusion of wisdom and drive." The left hand lightly resting on the wand alludes to "protecting established results."

At the center of the card stands the Home — Four of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. As head of logistics for the Day Wave Knights, Fulilanca's extraordinary quality lies in elevating "logistics" into the art of building a "home." The Wave Peak Fortress she oversaw is not only a fully functional military stronghold but a miniature community filled with humane care. From windshielded, sun-facing barracks and carefully calculated chimneys, to the "Homeland Viewing Platform" she insisted be built at every base — these details she persisted in together created a unique sense of belonging called "a home for our people." Four wands standing tall flutter with burning flames; from this place Fulilanca begins building the ideal home in her heart, symbolizing "a stable framework of achievement" and "incremental fulfillment." Flying bird decorations at the foreground's lower edge echo "the celebration of victory" and "community harmony." The star-shaped fence walls behind represent "a secure spiritual home" and "the destination of homecoming." The space separated by the fence from what lies beyond forms "the accessible path between reality and the ideal." Stars flickering continuously above reinforce "a carefree state of fulfillment." When action transforms through ordered structure into real achievement, life blossoms on a firm foundation into the most brilliant celebration.

At the center of the card stands the Calamity Dragon — Five of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In the Fourth Knights — the Calamity Dragon — Kreis embodies the Five of Wands, viewing obsessive power worship and internal competition as the only path to forging great warriors. His training bordered on life-or-death combat, frequently injuring comrades; he openly provoked at tactical meetings, treating harmony as an excuse for weaklings. This endless internal attrition eventually ignited a massive melee over spoils with the Second Knights, earning him severe disciplinary action. Yet the punishment became a turning point. In a bitter border bandit suppression, his reckless ferocity turned outward — single-handedly ripping open the enemy line to create an opening for his comrades — signaling that his Wand-Five fighting spirit was shifting from chaotic internal strife toward conquering external foes. In the open field, Kreis's wand clashes fiercely with four wands in the flames below — representing allied comrades. The dynamic of crossing wands corresponds to the white heat of clashing viewpoints. The roaring flames at the characters' feet echo the energy vortex ignited by conflict. Kreis standing and swinging embodies the courage to actively challenge. The nature of the apparent melee where no one is actually harmed reveals the essence of "constructive competition."

At the center of the card stands the Triumph — Six of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Elikael, deputy commander of the Day Wave Knights, is the perfect embodiment of the victory and glory symbolized by the Six of Wands. In the famous battle to suppress Duke Dulan's rebellion, she personally led cavalry in a crucial flanking maneuver through masterful command and personal valor, overturning the battle in a single stroke and becoming the kingdom's acknowledged symbol of victory. Yet her most outstanding quality lies in transforming personal glory into collective spiritual wealth — she insisted on letting common soldiers ride at the forefront of the triumphal procession and gave the honors to the families of fallen members. Triumphant Elikael holds the wand of victory and glory, returning home in honor after quelling the conflict — symbolizing "the coronation of victory" and "public recognition." The proud war horse beneath her represents "pure action force." Soldiers following with the same wands form "resonance of ideals" and "followers of a cause." Five wands laid crosswise behind the knight allude to "conquered challenges." The star-shaped necklace at her throat shows "the resolve to fight for one's beliefs." The flaming mane of the war horse against the simple white robe presents "the balance between passion and growth." The glittering laurel crown reinforces the peak state of honor.

At the center of the card stands the Swallowing Awn — Seven of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In the Battle of Throat-Cut Strait in year 971 of the Circular Calendar, when the main fleet was severely damaged, Golda of the Grey Whale Knights volunteered to lead three escort ships on the final rearguard defense mission. With extraordinary tactical willpower, she endured six hours of brutal combat, using overloaded Ethereal furnaces to create burning barriers that slowed the pursuing enemy. Faced with the extreme of ships destroyed and comrades falling one by one, she stood firm at the most dangerous bow, her will "as immovable as a reef." In the end, at the cost of near-total annihilation, she successfully protected the main force's safe withdrawal. Golda kneels on the ground, hands gripping her wand tight, gazing at six wands buried in the earth — representing six fallen comrades. This brutal victory brought her not only honor but grief too heavy to hide, symbolizing "active protection of what one has earned" and "fighting for one's beliefs." The six wands at her feet are both epitaphs for former comrades and testimony to the grueling battles she survived. Her position at the summit corresponds to "strategic initiative." The wand held vertically against her shoulder alludes to "building a defensive line centered on the self." The right hand not fully gripping tight reveals "the possibility of a counterattack hidden within defense."

At the center of the card stands the Shuttle — Eight of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In the Fifth Knights — the Blood Steed — messenger Talos is the embodiment of swiftness, precision, and the free flow of information. In the spring joint exercise of year 1004 of the Circular Calendar, faced with seventeen emergency orders issued in rapid succession over twelve hours, he and his mount "Shadow Shuttle" swept through treacherous terrain like a gale, simultaneously directing fellow knights, covering over eight hundred li — completing every delivery without error and providing real-time feedback on the dynamics of every unit based on keen observation, making subsequent command more precise. Eight wands represent the knights advancing rapidly toward their set target under messenger Talos's command — like arrows loosed from a bow slicing through the sky, presenting perfect parallel trajectories. They symbolize "the complete release of action force" and "high-speed progress after obstacles are cleared." The unified pointing of their tips corresponds to "the high focus on the target." The state of flying through the air represents "free action unbound." Flames enveloping the wands echo "the natural forward flow of life." The building in the distance hints at "a clearly visible endpoint." The clear sky and vast land form "an ideal environment for travel." The exquisite tips of various forms hint at "the precious value contained in action."

At the center of the card stands the Vigil — Nine of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In the Second Knights — the Night Cry — Auriq, who has served twenty-five years, is the embodiment of the tenacity and defensive wisdom of the Nine of Wands. Bearing eleven battle scars, his most outstanding achievement came in the extreme winter of year 991 of the Circular Calendar, when he infiltrated the northern rebel-occupied zone alone. Through instinctive blending with the environment and survival artistry beyond ordinary humans, he lurked in that desperate place for two months, ultimately bringing back the decisive intelligence that determined the course of the battle. Now he distills his lifetime of experience into the training manual The Vigilant Eye, whose core philosophy is "weaving vigilance into the bloodstream." Auriq stands in the night, holding tight to his wand, leaning on it — the countless scars and ailments have never broken this old sentinel, symbolizing "the vigilance born from enduring challenges" and "a defense that never slackens." The left hand on the wand and the hidden scars correspond to "the memory of past wounds," while his still highly alert posture shows "the heightened awareness born of tempering." Eight wands below him like a row of fence posts form "the protective barrier built by experience." Their uneven arrangement alludes to "the battle accumulation of different stages." His position at the highest point represents "the high ground of the mind."

At the center of the card stands the Mountain — Ten of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. The commander of the Grizzly Bear Knights, as representative of a tribe that surrendered, exemplifies the heavy burden symbolized by the Ten of Wands. He bears the multiple pressures of tribal survival, royal expectations, and knightly management, every decision feeling like being torn between different loyalties. In difficult moments such as the Black Rock Canyon battle, he must respond in real time to contradictory demands from every direction while fighting at the front. Yet assessment reports show his will is extraordinarily resilient — rooted in his unique path of balance: recording tribal proverbs in military regulations, weaving royal oaths into ceremonies. He proves that true strength lies not in setting down the burden but, for the sake of all one protects, standing straight-backed despite the unbearable weight. The stooped and trudging commander of the Grizzly Bear Knights shoulders ten wands and moves slowly forward, bearing immense pressure from every direction since he submitted to the crown, symbolizing "overextended responsibility" and "persisting under unbearable weight." Nine flame-patterned jewels burning among the wands represent the steadfastness and tenacity behind bearing pressure. The deeply bowed spine corresponds to "deformation under pressure." The stiff posture of arms wrapped around the wands represents "the stubbornness of refusing to let go." The undulating field underfoot echoes "the real tasks yet to be completed." The detail of bare feet on earth emphasizes "direct friction with reality."

At the center of the card stands the Deceive the Divine — Page of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. As a young apprentice personally tutored by Commander Rodwood, Sil demonstrates the Page of Wands' signature spirit of exploration and growth potential. He frequently proposes unconventional tactical concepts such as using the Ethereal Deceive the Divine to create "cognitive contamination" — most never adopted due to high risk, but core concepts like "perceptual fracture induction" have been incorporated into the strategic reserve. Under the commander's systematic training he has made significant progress in the delicate micro-control of illusions, able to keep error within a few seconds — though one incident that left squad members with a confused sense of direction also warns that his control still needs refinement. Currently he assists in perfecting the "mirror camouflage" project in the humble posture of a page, and his budding creativity, refined through systematic tempering, has the potential to become a pivotal variable that changes the battlefield in the future. The energetic young apprentice stands in the vast desert, his posture lightly gripping the wand embodying curiosity toward new beginnings and exploration. His billowing robe reflects the passion of the fire element; short hair beneath the robe reveals a pragmatic nature; a streamlined belt sash hints at inner wisdom and vitality. The flames bursting from the wand's tip correspond to the awakening of potential and new opportunities for growth. The circular flame wheel in the distance represents a goal not yet reached but clearly visible.

At the center of the card stands the Surge — Knight of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Knight Farmaro takes the swiftness and impact force symbolized by the Knight of Wands to their absolute limit. In the famous Battle of Iron River, he led his unit in an inconceivable raid — traversing a swamp thought impassable and launching a lethal strike at the enemy's weakest flank. Benefiting from the superhuman reaction speed granted by the Ethereal Falling Sun, he was able to process multiple streams of battlefield information with precision at the limit of a charge, making the unit function like a perfectly coordinated organism at high speed. As a radical in military philosophy, he firmly believes that "only the ever-advancing blade can dominate the battlefield." This blazing knight astride a charging falcon is enveloped in the flames his wand has become, symbolizing the complete release of action force and a clear directional goal — vowing to launch a strike that the enemy cannot possibly respond to. The swirling battle-garment shines with the pure energy of the fire element, fluttering like a flame itself, displaying unstoppable passion and courage. The falcon's mid-air leap corresponds to the speed of action and the resolve to break convention. The trailing flames beneath the wings testify to the powerful momentum of forward motion. The all-or-nothing posture with head held high echoes a soaring fighting spirit.

At the center of the card stands the Homeland — Queen of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Commander Melodar, through leadership rooted in deep emotional bonds, has forged the Grey Whale Knights into a whole filled with loyalty and conviction. She knows every crew member's name by heart, and at the crisis moment on a storm night she led from the front, crying "live or die with the Grey Whale" — earning the affectionate title "our commander." Tactically she shows sharpness beyond her years, such as precisely delegating command authority in the Battle of Broken Ice Bay to unleash the full fleet's initiative for coordinated combat. This mature woman holds her face resolute and upward, the sun-facing wand behind her symbolizing full acceptance and guidance of life's passion. She won over comrades who fought alongside her through her extraordinary personal charisma, and her vitality bound them into a solid whole. Her gleaming refined crown and robe are interwoven with the fire element's vitality and authority. Her hair curling like flame corresponds to vigorous life force and abundant creativity. The streamlined wand tip echoes inner courage and strength. The queen's steady posture reveals wisdom grounded in reality. The streamlined halo of light behind her holds both passion and protection. Her focused gaze ahead embodies a deep understanding of the meaning of action. When the fire element's energy manifests through a mature form, every action becomes a source nourishing life.

At the center of the card stands the Brain in the Shadow — King of Wands of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Commander Rodwood is the embodiment of the mature authority and strategic vision symbolized by the King of Wands, with "cognitive domain warfare" as the core of his command philosophy. The Red Rock Canyon battle he masterminded became a classic — drawing the enemy in through seventeen days of strategic deception and proving that "victory is decided before the horn sounds." In his hands, the Ethereal Deceive the Divine was elevated to a strategic weapon capable of weaving multiple layers of false intelligence, even using enemy spies in reverse to transmit disinformation — earning him the empress's title "Brain in the Shadow." He is equally dedicated to cultivating strategic talent, systematically imparting the art of deception. Rodwood has proven that the most powerful strength lies in the absolute mastery of wisdom; his gaze is always locked on the vast game beyond the horizon that ordinary commanders cannot see. This mature ruler holds a tilted wand, symbolizing precise mastery of action force and strategic guidance. His flame-burning helmet forms the classic iconography of the fire element. The golden ring crown burning above his head echoes the wisdom of combining action with patience. The unique and sharp wand together with the circular flame wheel focused on the wand in the background reinforce royal authority and wild power. His upright, resolute stance shows connection to earth energy. The burning sky and steady earth form a domain full of tension yet balanced. His gaze fixed on the distance betrays the farsight of a strategist.

At the center of the image stands 【Ethereal Holy Grail】 from the Yizhu world, the Ace of Cups. It is a device crafted by the Four Directions Academy for storing large amounts of information, but all were stolen in an accident; searching for the scattered Grails remains an important task for Academy members to this day. The Ace of Cups symbolizes a completely new beginning of emotion and spirit: the Grail floating quietly in the clouds represents "the gift of divine grace" and "the opening of the subconscious." The five streams flowing from the cup and gathering below correspond to "the awakening of the five senses" and "the abundant flow of emotion." The white dove flying into the cup, holding a star ray, symbolizes "nourishment of the soul" and "the revelation of peace." The swallows spiraling around the cup echo "the pure state of the subconscious" and "the sprouting of spiritual growth." The grooves carved on the cup body like undulating water flows suggest "the channel between the material world and the spiritual world." These elements together interpret the essence of the Ace of Cups as "the source of love" — when divine power pours through the Grail, the soul will break all bondage and nurture infinite possibility in the fertile soil of emotion.

At the center of the image stand 【Clarissa & Leona】 from the Yizhu world, the Two of Cups. Academy linguist 【Clarissa】 and cryptographer 【Leona】 work closely together, jointly deciphering the inscriptions on the bases of Grails numbered 2 and 3, and after reaching consensus, submit a report to the Academy. The Two of Cups symbolizes an emotionally equal and harmonious bond: the two facing each other with cups hold equal postures, dividing labor in cooperative decipherment of the Grail inscriptions — representing "resonance of souls" and "bidirectional emotional flow." The tilted cups in their hands form an exchange arc, corresponding to "the blending of hearts" and "the balance of energy." The water columns surging from the cups meeting in the air symbolize "emotional resonance" and "the igniting of inspiration." The gesture of the two trying to touch each other suggests "the cooperation of consciousness and subconsciousness." The star-shaped backdrop below manifests "the harmonization of opposing forces" and "the magic of communication." The cipher stones above their heads correspond to "the taming of raw passion" and "spiritual elevation." The distant mountains form "the solid foundation of an emotional relationship." The contrasting black and white of their robes represents "the dialectical unity of passion and purity." These elements together interpret the essence of the Two of Cups: "soul contract."

At the center of the image stands 【The Celebration】 from the Yizhu world, the Three of Cups. Academy botanist 【Gaia】, chemist 【Beatrice】, and metallurgist 【Theodora】 submit a new interdisciplinary research plan to reconstruct the physical composition of the Grail through modern materials science. After a lengthy collaboration, the three finally produce three nearly identical Grails, though their storage capacity and duration are greatly reduced; while the replication is not entirely successful, the collaboration still accumulates precious production experience for the Academy. The Three of Cups symbolizes celebration, communion, and abundant results: the synchronized posture of the three Academy ladies raising their cups represents "community celebration" and "the blending of emotional energy." The cups touching in their hands form a solid triangle, corresponding to "stable emotional connection" and "the joy of multilateral cooperation." The 【Ethereal Focus】 — the water-flow crown spiraling above the three ladies' heads — can calm the mind and concentrate attention, symbolizing "material harvest" and "spiritual joy." The water flows surrounding them echo "nature's gift" and "proof of abundance." The dancing posture with upturned faces suggests "gratitude for the gifts of life." The environment enclosed by a ring valley forms "a safe, shared space for growth." These elements interpret the essence of the Three of Cups: "harvest feast."

At the center of the image stands 【Malvina's Rejection】 from the Yizhu world, the Four of Cups. Senior Academy researcher 【Malvina】 refuses the 【Pathfinder】 project arranged by the Academy and instead launches an independent "Legacy Treasure" research plan, wanting to restore the Academy's glory by tracing the vast web of knowledge once stored in the Grails, rather than simply searching for the Grails as physical knowledge vessels. The Four of Cups symbolizes introspection, sediment, and the examination of opportunity: Malvina hesitating and contemplating under a tree, in a closed posture unwilling to move forward, corresponds to "the temporary closing of the emotional world" and "the state of inner reflection." The three Grails arranged before her symbolize "existing emotional choices," their orderly arrangement suggesting "the lack of novelty in the present state." The fourth Grail drifting out from the clouds represents "a sudden new opportunity." Malvina hesitantly avoiding all the Grails corresponds to "deliberate detachment from the present state and opportunities." The misty hills in the background constitute "unexplored life possibilities." The lush trees manifest "the continuous growth of inner life." These elements reveal the essence of the Four of Cups: "the soul's dormant period."

At the center of the image stands 【The False Grail】 from the Yizhu world, the Five of Cups. Academy analyst 【Hortensia】 takes charge of five Grail fragments the Academy expended enormous effort to locate, and after a series of precise experiments, she definitively identifies three of them as forgeries. This discovery by Hortensia causes a massive sensation; the Pathfinder project is temporarily ordered to halt, and people are immersed in the grief of having spent enormous effort, time, and money searching for false Grails. The core meaning of the Five of Cups is "focusing on loss" and "ignoring remaining support": Hortensia in a black cloak turning her back to the viewer symbolizes "immersion in grief" and "closing off from the outside." The three overturned cups before her — the false Grails — represent "loss that has occurred" and "emotional frustration." The two cups still standing behind her, unnoticed by the figure, correspond to "ignored positive resources" and "latent emotional support." The winding river at her feet suggests "the continuous flow of emotion" and "healing brought by time." The bridge over the river toward a distant building symbolizes "the path to rebuilding connection" and "hope for the future." These elements reveal the core insight of the Five of Cups: in loss, we often focus too much on the overturned cups and fail to see the grace and new possibilities that still stand firm in life.

At the center of the image stands 【Adelaide's Gift】 from the Yizhu world, the Six of Cups. In Circular Calendar year 835, retired researcher Adelaide donates to the Four Directions Academy notes she spent more than thirty years collecting on folk legends, rituals, and customs related to the "Holy Grail," and designates her apprentice Rosalind to collate only 5 pages per day to maximize the accuracy of the original records. These notes systematically reveal that the Holy Grail in folk narrative primarily symbolizes three major themes: abundance and agricultural knowledge, healing and medical formulas, and wisdom and revelatory mysteries. The core meaning of the Six of Cups is "innocent giving," "nostalgic warmth," and "protected beauty": Adelaide bestowing knowledge upon apprentice Rosalind in the courtyard symbolizes "the exchange of innocent emotion" and "unconditional giving." The Grail the elder passes to the younger, flowing with clear water, corresponds to "the transmission of emotional nourishment" and "the sharing of beautiful memories." The five other neatly arranged Grails represent "an abundant reserve of emotion" and "ordered memories of the past." The tranquil environment constitutes "a protected, safe space." The winding path leading away reminds one of "the inevitable growth of eventually stepping out of the comfort zone." These elements interpret the essence of the Six of Cups: revisiting beauty and transmitting warmth in a safe harbor, while knowing that this tranquility will ultimately lead us toward a broader world.

At the center of the image stands 【The Choice】 from the Yizhu world, the Seven of Cups. In Circular Calendar year 838, leading Academy scholar Octavia, overseeing the allocation of research funds for Grail studies, designs an anonymous weighted scoring process. However, she ultimately exercises her power of decision, overturning the "Material Analysis" project with the highest total score among seven projects and instead awarding the main funds to the new "Knowledge Container Content Research" proposal ranked fourth. The Seven of Cups' core meaning is "the confusion of desire," "the emergence of illusions," and "inner choice": the seven cups appearing in the mist each carry different symbols — the veiled glowing humanoid corresponds to "projection of spiritual idols," the flickering building symbolizes "unattainable ambition," the upright staff represents "the temptation of power," the star-shaped gem suggests "material desire," the gleaming laurel corresponds to "worldly achievement," the snake implies "hidden fears," and the quietly perching crow foreshadows "an unformed persona." The enveloping gray mist symbolizes "the chaotic subconscious." The posture of the watching dark figure with open hands embodies "the state of passive reception" and "lack of active filtering." These elements reveal the essence of the Seven of Cups: only by clearing away the mist for sober discernment can one transform illusory projections into real life choices.

At the center of the image stands 【Ash Star】 from the Yizhu world, the Eight of Cups. In Circular Calendar year 841, researcher Josefa proposes a hypothesis that astrological cycles influence the Holy Grail's "revelations," but receives no support as it diverges from the mainstream. She then enters an abandoned observatory with personal resources, independently launching research through continuous astronomical observation and experiments with 【Ash Matter】 samples she brought herself. Over about 14 months, she shifts focus from Grails to Ash Matter, discovering that its energy fluctuations intensify under specific constellations. During the 843 plague she refuses to return and ultimately dies of illness, but leaves behind complete observation records of over 800 days, which decades later become foundational documents for this cross-disciplinary field. The core meaning of the Eight of Cups is "purposeful departure," "the pursuit of deeper meaning," and "the courage to cross the comfort zone": the eight neatly arranged Grails symbolize "emotional achievements already attained" and "a stable present state that has grown wearisome." Josefa turning her back to the Grails and walking away represents "clear-eyed abandonment" and "pursuit of higher value." The darkness flowing in the distance suggests "a solitary journey of growth." The brilliant path in the polar day and stars gleaming in the eternal night manifest "the guidance of intuition" and "the call of the subconscious." These elements reveal the essence of the Eight of Cups: when the soul hears the call of the distance, the most courageous act is often to leave the seemingly perfect surface and seek life's deeper answers while journeying alone.

At the center of the image stands 【The Atlas】 from the Yizhu world, the Nine of Cups. In Circular Calendar year 845, reclusive scholar Isadora submits a revolutionary research report to the Four Directions Academy. To resolve the complex and contradictory records in the field of Grail research, rather than conducting new investigations, she creates a nine-dimensional classification method, standardizing and encoding hundreds of core documents, and constructing a multidimensional relational atlas system. She rejects the personal honors that follow, insisting the atlas's value lies in being a "living tool" that requires continuous updating, emphasizing that "knowledge is not a static treasure but a flowing river." The Nine of Cups is known as the "wish fulfilled" card: Isadora at the center with arms outstretched symbolizes "the completeness of self-realization" and "confirmation of inner abundance." The nine cups arranged in an arc behind her correspond to "the ultimate fulfillment of emotional wishes" and "the complete manifestation of cosmic grace." The gorgeous attire adorned with star chains manifests "the celebration of worldly achievement" and "the blossoming of life's passion." The radiant star rising from the cup behind symbolizes "deep satisfaction of the subconscious." The platform displaying the Grails constitutes the sense of a stage where "achievement is objectively witnessed." These elements interpret the essence of the Nine of Cups: "wishes coming true."

At the center of the image stands 【Remnant Dust Resonance】 from the Yizhu world, the Ten of Cups. In Circular Calendar year 802, senior steward of the Four Directions Academy Elvira oversees the final evaluation of the "Remnant Dust Resonance" project. The project aims to use modulated "Ethereal Ash" to allow the bereaved to have one last complete family conversation within three days while the soul is soul-bound, achieving emotional reconciliation. In the evaluation of blacksmith widow Marta's family, family members' "grief index" significantly decreases as they complete rituals with the deceased such as listening to family stories and singing hymns. The Ten of Cups is the ultimate symbol of emotional fulfillment and earthly paradise: ten Grails hanging beneath a gorgeous rainbow in the sky, with Elvira using specially crafted Ethereal Ash to reunite the deceased with the living, corresponding to "the descent of divine blessing" and "the realization of perfect emotion." The embracing couple and the children gazing at each other form the core family unit, symbolizing "the crystallization of love" and "the inheritance of emotion." The shining starlight in the distance constitutes "a rich natural support system." These elements interpret the essence of the Ten of Cups: "earthly paradise" — when individual happiness is sublimated into collective harmony, emotional connection transcends the personal sphere and creates eternal beauty.

At the center of the image stands 【Myriad String Resonance】 from the Yizhu world, the Page of Cups. In Circular Calendar year 885, trainee researcher Lina, during routine testing, uses a high-frequency tone out of personal interest to stimulate Holy Grail number 56 — 【Ethereal Holy Grail】 — and unexpectedly observes stable, regular anomalous energy fluctuations whose patterns resemble unknown coding. Through repeated experiments she confirms this phenomenon to be a secondary resonance property unique to that Grail. Rather than reporting through normal channels, Lina presents the complete record directly to senior researcher Sofia, known for her open-minded thinking, proposing in her report that this might become "the foundation for another form of communication." This discovery, initially classified as a "minor observation," eventually becomes the starting point for developing non-standard encrypted communication technology. The Page of Cups is a symbol of budding emotion and the awakening of intuition: trainee researcher Lina gazing intently at Grail #56 — being stimulated by high-frequency tones — and observing its anomalous energy fluctuations symbolizes "the awakening of emotional awareness" and "the exploration of the subconscious domain." The anomalous energy ripples leaping from the cup correspond to "the eruption of inspiration" and "the manifestation of subconscious messages." The waves behind represent "the fluctuations of the emotional world" and "the flow of intuition." These elements interpret the essence of the Page of Cups: "spiritual messenger."

At the center of the image stands 【Seraphina's Purification】 from the Yizhu world, the Knight of Cups. Faced with a plague in a border village caused by water source contamination, Triangle Church-stationed knight Seraphina goes against the Academy's convention of prioritizing internal protection, actively proposing to deploy the 【Ethereal Purgation】 device and executing a purification mission using the method recorded in Holy Grail number 57. Though the proposal passes only after heated debate with strict conditions, she still personally leads a squad to successfully repel bandits and purify the water source, controlling the epidemic. In her report she argues for its long-term value as "seventy-four lives saved," and though viewed as defiance, this action successfully pushes the Academy's subsequent adjustment of limited external aid policy, and the people praise her as "Seraphina's Purification." The Knight of Cups is a symbol of poetic ideals and romantic action: Seraphina seated upright on billowing water flows, cup in hand, moving forward, symbolizes "the concrete realization of emotional pursuit" and "the practice of lofty ideals." The cup held flat in her hand like an offering toward the distance corresponds to "emotional dedication" and "focused attention on spiritual goals." The elegant, dynamic billowing water flows represent "the steady flow of emotional energy." These elements interpret the essence of the Knight of Cups: "seeker of the soul."

At the center of the image stands 【Shared Emotions】 from the Yizhu world, the Queen of Cups. In Circular Calendar year 808, faced with the tension within the Academy caused by Grail allocation, Monica, head of the "Healing Sanctuary," does not resort to conventional mediation but instead launches an innovative psychological intervention. She invites members of both sides to meditate with the assistance of weakly powered star-stone arrays, and through analyzing the imagery and emotions in their subconsciouses, she discerns that the root of the conflict is a universally present anxiety about "future security." Her work pioneers entirely new perspectives and tools for the Academy in handling internal psychological dynamics. The Queen of Cups is the ultimate embodiment of the yin face of the water element: Monica seated at center, projecting her consciousness onto a giant sculpture and gazing at the Grail in her hands, symbolizes "absolute sovereignty over the emotional world" and "deep immersion in intuitive power." The gently cradled cup represents "the protected source of intuition" and "the inner restraint of emotional energy." The water spiraling upward in the cup corresponds to "the sublimation of spiritual messages." The fluid-form crown manifests "the natural gift of emotional wisdom." The ripple of radiance below constitutes the metaphor of "disturbing the sea of emotion with the mind." These elements interpret the essence of the Queen of Cups: "master of intuition."

At the center of the image stands 【Constance's Integration】 from the Yizhu world, the King of Cups. In Circular Calendar year 849, Academy leader 【Constance】 oversees the compilation of the "Holy Grail Research Standards." He integrates the research achievements of the previous 32 years, establishing standardized Grail verification procedures, document citation norms, and data recording formats. In the final version, he removes all expressions with mystical tendencies, clearly defining the Grail as "the physical carrier of sixth-century knowledge storage technology." This standard becomes the operational norm for Grail research of later generations. The King of Cups is a perfect fusion of emotional wisdom and spiritual authority: the Academy leader seated steadily on the throne, holding the Grail with a composed demeanor, determined to use his knowledge to integrate the complex knowledge system of the Grails, symbolizes "absolute mastery over the emotional world" and "the embodiment of spiritual power." His flowing-form throne behind him, undulating but steady as a rock, corresponds to "the wisdom of maintaining composure amid emotional tides." The closed Grail he holds represents "introverted emotional depth" and "the treasuring of intuitive power." The gleaming laurel above his head manifests "leadership in the spiritual domain." The churning white threads behind him are the external manifestation of his inner world. These elements interpret the essence of the King of Cups: "helmsman of emotion."

At the center of the card stands the承冕 — Sword One of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Former royal guard captain Raizak was sentenced as one of the Impure in 867 and exiled. He initially sought legal redress through the Redemption Committee, but every petition was rejected. In 871, his wife and children died during the march because their escort refused to intervene, destroying his last willingness to compromise. He announced he sought only reckoning. That same year he led an ambush on a church patrol and seized the shapeshifting weapon Ethereal Stormlight, founding the First House — House承冕 — and gathering radical resisters, marking the shift of the Impure movement from political petition to armed resistance. A sharp, radiant vertical sword pierces a crown — just as Raizak's Ethereal Stormlight seeks to shatter royal chains. The straight double-edged blade embodies absolute reason and the decisiveness that severs confusion; the golden crown at its tip marks the collapse of old belief systems. Spiraling new leaves form an infinity shape — endless possibility born from a mind reborn. The vast distant summit hints at a clear spiritual goal; the pure sky mirrors the purity of truth.

At the center of the card stands the 不見 — Sword Two of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Ingtinayi possessed both the scar of the Impure and a miracle stigma simultaneously, making her a living specimen of "double defilement" in the church's eyes. Her parents were executed; she herself endured cruel experiments in the research institute that left her blind and her left hand crippled. In the winter of 900, she used the Bladeless miracle to escape and founded the Second House — House 不見 — in Shuangyuan. Though blind, her invisible blade and absolute will for revenge made her one of the most radical and unpredictable leaders among the Thirteen Houses. Blindfolded Ingtinayi stands clutching twin swords at a moonlit shore, her hatred clouding the inner sight she no longer possesses. The two crossed blades before her chest embody the deadlock of opposing thoughts; the white cloth binding her eyes is the act of self-blinding — refusing truth. Dark waves churn behind her, hinting at suppressed emotional undertow. The crescent moon above casts dim light, deepening the fog of perception. Her rigid posture speaks of a taut psychological defense, and the oppressive scene carries the chill of frozen feeling.

At the center of the card stands the 斥羽 — Sword Three of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Nordest was born of an union between one of the Impure and a church believer. At his birth, an uncontrolled Sublimation miracle killed his mother. His father gave him to the church as an experimental subject from childhood. After growing up he broke free, killed his father in revenge, and finally reached Shuangyuan. His unique flight ability and fighting style made him leader of the Third House — House 斥羽 — yet the wounds buried deep within and his isolating nature made it impossible for him to truly belong. A vivid red heart pierced by three swords hangs in a storm-dark sky — the image of Nordest's shattered despair: his own miracle ran wild and killed his mother; his father sacrificed him; at last hatred coiled around him and drove him to slay the very man who gave him life. The three blades in triangular formation stand for layered trauma from compounding blows. Rain traces on the hilts evoke grief still fermenting. Heavy dark clouds declare the inevitability of emotional release. Blazing fire behind the heart connects pain to lived reality. Each blade strikes from a different angle — mother, father, and self.

At the center of the card stands the 魘寐 — Sword Four of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. As a child, Lauterhoi was taken in by the widow Ulnera. When his identity as one of the Impure was exposed, Ulnera died at the church's hands trying to protect him. After his exile to Shuangyuan, revenge became his sole reason to exist. He ambushed and killed the knight Laurens, seizing the weapon Ethereal Wailing — capable of conjuring mental nightmares — and founded the Fourth House, House 靨寐. Because the Thirteenth House master Su Kris had also lost a vital protector to church persecution, the two forged a deep strategic and emotional alliance rooted in shared trauma and hatred, healing together the vast wounds beneath. In the image Lauterhoi rests still in a quiet chamber, quieting and healing the layers of suffering the church inflicted on him. His motionless form lying in the stone coffin embodies the necessary pause of withdrawing from battle; closed eyes speak of deep introspection and energy recovery. Flowing lines rising from his head hint at spiritual guidance and nourishment of the soul. Three suspended swords below represent conflicts set aside for now; the fourth sword within reach to his right speaks of a defense that can resume at any moment.

At the center of the card stands the 無勝 — Sword Five of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Vantro took delight in collecting enemy weapons, frequently missing battle opportunities because he was too busy seizing arms, until in 891 he ambushed the knight captain Dergnis hoping to steal the famed blade Ethereal Sharp Edge — only to be countered, losing his right arm. That defeat gave him the revelation: "no victory is victory." He fitted a steam-mechanical prosthetic, renamed his house 無勝 — House of No Victory — and from then on abandoned hollow triumphs, focusing on practical tactics, becoming one of the most pragmatic and inscrutable commanders among the Thirteen Houses. In the image, victor Vantro holds three swords and gazes down at defeated opponents; his obsession with seizing enemy weapons never diminished regardless of the cost to the battle. The fractured, gloomy sky symbolizes the spiritual wasteland after conflict. The winner's casual posture against the fleeing backs of the defeated makes a dramatic contrast between winner and loser. Two swords scattered on the sand represent broken trust and severed bonds. The sharp peaks in the background echo unquiet emotional aftershocks and hint at the hidden cost of victory.

At the center of the card stands the 曳渡 — Sword Six of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Shaga Lan grew up on the southeastern coast and was a master of water. In 891, when her identity as one of the Impure was revealed, church forces burned her home and killed her father. Using her intimate knowledge of waterways she escaped successfully to Shuangyuan. Carrying the Sacrifice miracle, she founded the Sixth House — House 曳渡 — and frequently offered herself as bait to open secret supply lines and evacuation routes for the Impure, her strategic worth far exceeding her combat strength. A small boat carries the cloaked Shaga Lan slowly toward the far shore. The surging sea became her refuge from pursuit — those unfamiliar with water dared not follow, and could only watch her receding figure. She stands at the bow looking out at the water, unable for now to quiet the grief in her heart. The six swords standing upright at the bow represent old wounds already faced but not yet dissolved. The ferryman's steady composure embodies calm and professional guidance. Shaga Lan, cloaked and head bowed, silently accepts the pain. The plain sky traces the arc from depression toward hope.

At the center of the card stands the 盜光 — Sword Seven of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. The master of the Seventh House — House 盜光 — is the most mysterious leader among the Thirteen Houses: no record exists of identity, appearance, or origins. Their existence is confirmed only through a series of thefts targeting the church and the royal house. The core ability is incomparable infiltration — exploiting psychological blind spots in security systems and procedural gaps, moving with swift silence and leaving no trace.
