The most famous operation was the theft of the weapon Ethereal Thorn Net from the weapons scholar Dr. Olanden, a blade that returns all damage doubled. Though small in scale, House 盜光 is a critical enabler for the Thirteen Houses, steadily supplying weapons and intelligence, and its existence alone is a continuous mockery of the system. In the image, 盜光 slips silently away from a military camp, already carrying five sharp swords in the shadows behind them, noticed by no one. The triumphant posture of stealing five blades in darkness embodies the instant success of outsmarting an opponent for resources. Two straight swords left in the camp represent unseen latent danger. The alert backward glance conceals vigilance against pursuit. The grey buildings and rolling mountains form the blurred boundary between enemy and ally territory.

At the center of the card stands the 荊籬 — Sword Eight of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Su Kris, a descendant of both a royal duke and a church believer, was found to carry both the Impure scar and the Mind-Sight scar simultaneously, stripped of every privilege and exiled to Shuangyuan. Over five years his mind deteriorated steadily, falling into madness and anguish, and he found deep resonance with the Fourth House master Lauterhoi, who bore similar trauma. In this state he founded the Eighth House — House 荊籬 — the name evoking a painful self-constructed barrier of thorns. The Mind-Sight miracle may compound his mental burden, making his actions unpredictable; he currently relies mainly on his alliance with House 靨寐 for support. Blindfolded and bound, Su Kris stands in a predicament that seems to offer no exit, as if a monstrous pain is always ready to devour him. His head bowed deeply downward embodies a self-deception that refuses to see clearly. Arms rigidly bound speak of the mind imprisoning its own inner strength. Eight swords planted around him form the bars of a mental cage; their tips driven into muddy earth evoke the paralysis of rigid thinking. Flowing mist rising alongside the blades hints at the ignored possibility of emotional movement. The discomfort of standing barefoot marks the sting of reality's edge.

At the center of the card stands the 刑境 — Sword Nine of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Loren Velde, master of the Ninth House — House 刑境 — is the most hidden existence among the Thirteen Houses: name, appearance, and past are all completely erased, making him a walking enigma. Using the weapon Ethereal Rain Face he can perfectly alter his appearance and voice, and has never appeared as his true self. This ability allows him to deeply infiltrate every faction, gathering core intelligence exclusively for the Thirteen Houses. He has a working relationship with House 盜光 but they do not trust each other. His continuous concealment may itself be outward evidence of an inner pain of the Sword Nine variety — threat level is extreme. In the image Loren Velde jolts awake in deep night from a nightmare, tormented by fear of his true interior — that hidden truth he has never shown to anyone. The figure sitting bolt upright on a stone platform, face covered by both hands, embodies the helplessness of being broken by inner terror. Nine swords arrayed on the wall behind him stand like blades of judgment, representing dense negative thinking and unresolved mental pressure. The twisting upward wave of his mental world alludes to the projection of unconscious fear. Secret runes carved behind him echo ongoing inner conflict. Flames and smoke rising from the sword blades magnify the isolation and abandonment of his inner state.

At the center of the card stands the 救刃 — Sword Ten of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Waili Telga, formerly a warden at Black Rock Prison, was exiled to Shuangyuan when his scar was exposed, enduring the revenge of former prisoners. In that extremity, using the weapon Ethereal Ten Blades he founded the Tenth House — House 救刃 — whose name means "using blades to stop harm." He transformed from a ruthless keeper of order into an even more ruthless avenger, and with his deep knowledge of the system and hatred embedded to the bone became a razor-sharp mockery of and grave threat to the imperial and church establishment. In the image the prone Waili Terga is pierced by ten sharp swords — not a literally existing scene, but a true portrait of his inner despair: a civil servant who once conscientiously upheld his duty to the crown, subjected to every betrayal imaginable. Ten swords driven into his back spread in a fan, symbolizing the fate blow of total encirclement and the inescapable ending. His rigid prone form and pale face buried in dust reflect the complete collapse of an old life pattern. The pitch-black sky and horizon form an eerie intermingling of despair and hope. Dawn rising in the distance hints at a chance of rebirth at the end of destruction.

At the center of the card stands the 皆見 — Page of Swords of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Shute Outrans, descendant of one of the Impure and a believer, simultaneously carries the stigmas of Mind-Sight, Shell-Shedding, and Impure — making him a long-time captive of passive mind-reading. To hide his identity he self-immolated to destroy his face, but was exposed in 891 during an inspection when his mental irregularity could not be concealed. He used a false-death technique to escape to Shuangyuan and founded the Eleventh House — House 皆見. Using his ability to peer into minds he wove an enormous intelligence network, becoming the indispensable "eyes" of the Thirteen Houses. Young Shute Outrans stands on a hilltop facing the wind, coolly contemplating his current situation. Both hands lightly grip an upright sword in the classic pose of the "alert messenger." Strange ornaments fluttering in the wind behind him symbolize the lively flow of his mental energy; the influence of passive mind-reading makes his thinking too diffuse and constantly vigilant. The careful grip speaks of devout seeking of truth. The rolling moon phases at his feet represent the grounded reality of intellectual growth. Tumultuous flames behind him hint at messages arriving from afar. The sword's cold gleaming edge shines with a rationality unblurred by emotion.

At the center of the card stands the 聽塵 — Knight of Swords of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. After experiencing the Cicada God Calling event, Roy Makma's hearing underwent a profound change — gaining transcendent hearing at the permanent cost of his voice. Using this ability and the silent weapon Ethereal Gauze Wing he can precisely locate and deliver lethal strikes by listening to the micro-sounds of the environment, founding the Twelfth House — House 聽塵 — specializing in reconnaissance and assassination, becoming a sharp and solitary "silent blade" among the Thirteen Houses. In the image, the galloping knight Roy Makma raises his sword and charges on horseback, his transcendent hearing — gifted by the Cicada God — guiding him to strike the enemy base by surprise. The horse leaping into air embodies the extreme speed of thought converted into action. The cloak whipping in wild wind matches the explosive release of mental energy. The raised gleaming sword represents the decisiveness to cut through all confusion. Air currents rising and swirling around the blade allude to an unbound free will. The horse's tightly shut eyes reveal raw untamed momentum. The blade's track slicing through clouds hints at the attempt to tear emotional fog apart with reason.

At the center of the card stands the 流天 — Queen of Swords of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Lanzhoma was originally an elite of the church's White Triangle. When she touched the sacred relic "Primordial Triangle," an Impure scar suddenly appeared on her chest and she was arrested and sentenced. Thanks to colleagues who helped her break out, she fled to Shuangyuan. Wielding the weapon Ethereal Remnant Leaf she founded the Thirteenth House — House 流天 — and became the strategic arbiter of the Thirteen Houses, combining wisdom with authority, the lethal opponent the church created with its own hands. Wise Lanzhoma gazes at her sword, calculating how to preserve as much of the living force as possible and extract it from the entire battle zone. The Thirteen Houses have been fleeing for a long time; it is always Lanzhoma's rational planning and analysis that finds the exit from each desperate corner. Her upright and elegant bearing symbolizes a plane of thought above worldly concerns. The hand lightly touching the sword's edge embodies precise mastery of truth. A floating, shimmering crown suggests the mind's transformative power. The lifted grip of her left hand shows all-encompassing insight. The fluid lining of her cloak echoes the flowing nature of her thought. The cold blade represents a gaze that pierces appearances. The clear sky behind her and the jagged cliff beneath her feet form an eternal dialogue between emotion and reason.

At the center of the card stands the 見真 — King of Swords of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. House 見真 is the supreme and utterly secret decision-making core behind the Thirteen Houses; its true identity and form of existence are both blank. Strategic orders are issued only through the First House master Raizak as the sole channel, ensuring authority and concealment. Records show it directly intervened at only three major historical junctures, and each time it turned the tide — but its specific means cannot be reconstructed to this day. Its strategic designs are far-reaching, precise, and efficient, capable of maximizing the coordination of each House's unique strengths. As the brain and soul of the Impure organization, House 見真 is the "supreme threat" most feared by both the church and the imperial house. The imposing House 見真 holds an unsheathed sword with both hands, about to drive down another pivot-point that will determine the fate of the Thirteen Houses. His true face is forever hidden in shadow, yet invisibly shapes the entire battlefield. The straight double-edged sword symbolizes absolute reason that cuts through falsehood. A crown standing upright like inverted thorns corresponds to a clarity of mind sharp as ice. A short dagger encircled by thorns tilted above alludes to the transcendence of thought in transformation. Wings folded from behind the figure to the front echo a spiritual energy held in reserve. The stance with feet enclosed in a cage of sword blades shows the firm connection between thought and reality.

At the center of the card stands the 星幣 — Ace of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 381 of the Circular Calendar, Star Stones were first discovered in the town of Kisaude, with the unique property of changing color between day and night — hard yet brittle. By 451 the church found that Star Stones could resonate with defective miracle circuits and dramatically restore their function, a discovery it chose to keep secret. In 488, alchemist Fusmelo extracted from them the key substance Ash Matter, which the church subsequently cast into the shape of standard coins — Star Coins — primarily as a symbol of internal church power. From Ash Matter they developed Ethereal Ash in 566, capable of briefly trapping a soul. In 723, the Four Directions Academy obtained the production method through an undercover agent. With the discovery of a major southwestern ore belt in 766, Star Stone output surged, but the symbolic power of Star Coins declined after 1023 when miracle circuits were stripped away. This card symbolizes a new beginning and unlimited potential in the material world. A stone wall rising from the earth holds aloft a gleaming Star Coin — a tangible gift and opportunity granted by the cosmos. Its symmetrical balanced form mirrors the perfect equilibrium of elemental forces, and the star-ring decoration around its edge hints at the cyclical law of natural growth. Birds circle below, echoing the harmony of desire and spirit. The mountain ranges beyond the wall form a clear distant goal; the smooth stone-paved path is the viable way to reach it.

In the image, Marta clad in flowing gauze is juggling two Star Coins, lost in deep thought about how to balance the two choices before her. Her posture and surroundings reveal the core mystery of "dynamic equilibrium": the Star Coins cycling ceaselessly through her hands symbolize the constant fluctuation of resources and opportunities; the billowing wave-like gauze at her sides hints at the inevitable turbulence of fate; the soft, white, ever-shifting fabric speaks of the flexibility needed when roles must change; and the subtle balancing of both hands shows a composure that adapts to change. All these elements together express the essence of the Two of Pentacles: in the tides of fate, true mastery lies not in eliminating fluctuation but in cultivating the wisdom to dance with it — making every swaying moment a chance to recalibrate the center of one's life.

At the center of the card stands the Pannofierre Pillar — Three of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 701 of the Circular Calendar, to restore the central pillar of an ancient church hall — the Pannofierre Pillar — craftsperson Elvie (White Triangle), inscription master Beatrice (White Triangle), and theologian Sofia (Black Triangle) formed a temporary workshop. Elvie was responsible for restoring the pillar's base using Star Stone powder mixed with mithril; Beatrice proofread and re-carved the inscriptions; Sofia consulted historical records to compare and correct the overall form. The three cross-checked each other's progress daily, and the restoration lasted three months — bringing the pillar back in near-perfect form. In the image the three figures collaborate closely beneath an unfinished church arch: the inscription master holds the design and guides the direction, the craftsperson applies the chisel with careful artistry, and the theologian provides scholarly support. The golden triangle they form perfectly expresses the essence of professional collaboration. Three Star Coins hovering at the vault crown bear witness to the crystallization of skill. The scaffolding below and the great sphere in the background correspond to the building of solid foundations. The outline of a stained window hints at a brilliant future vision about to bloom.

At the center of the card stands the 否決 — Four of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 744 of the Circular Calendar, Star Coin vault administrator Anastasiya rejected the royal request to extract Ash Matter in bulk to produce Ethereal Ash, insisting on its scarcity. Ten years later she further reinforced security, establishing a three-key co-managed gate and personally counting stock each day, ensuring that over a forty-year tenure vault losses remained below 0.5% — guarding the Star Coin inventory with absolute rigor. In the image, Anastasiya crowned with a star tiara sits clasping Star Coins in a lonely citadel, having fallen into near-obsessive territory in her mission to protect them. The glittering crown above and the Star Coins fixed beneath her body symbolize total defensive entrenchment around existing achievement. The coins she clutches to her chest are held as if guarding the source of life itself. The thick smoke behind her becomes a magnificent cage of self-isolation. Her rigid posture and guarded expression betray deep security anxiety. All these elements together paint the contradictory nature of the Four of Pentacles' "guardian": when the obsession with security exceeds the need for growth, stability mutates into bondage — only by finding balance between holding tight and letting go can wealth and vital energy truly flow.

At the center of the card stands the 焰方 — Five of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In the harsh winter of year 788 of the Circular Calendar, a northern outpost fell into crisis when coal ran out and fifteen White Triangle members froze to death. Black Triangle Yolanda resolute gave the ritual object "Flame Square" priority for warming the wounded rather than the chapel, personally going to the disaster zone at the cost of three frostbitten fingers. Though reprimanded by the Red Triangle and fined her wages, her humanitarian act was remembered by the common people and recorded in the Records of the Triangle Church. On a bitter wind-and-snow night, church members at the northern outpost are plunged into the terror of extreme cold; two of them stumble past a stone wall carved with Star Coins. Their predicament against their surroundings reveals a profound parable of "material hardship and spiritual dawn": the lame elder's crutch and the bundled woman's torn shoes make material poverty tangible; the blizzard echoes the harsh reality of life's adversity; yet the Star Coins on the wall not yet fully buried by ice and snow allude to an overlooked spiritual refuge — their flickering star patterns are precisely the fire of hope that never extinguished amid suffering. The two figures supporting each other embody an emotional bond that transcends the material. And in the end they truly did receive the Flame Square that Yolanda sent.

At the center of the card stands the 施予 — Six of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. During the plague of year 822 of the Circular Calendar, charity director Claudia distributed medicine not strictly according to the Red Triangle Bruena's orders — which ranked distribution by tax records — but according to the severity of wounds and illness. This approach saved multiple marginal families while actually improving popular acceptance of the church. In the image Claudia distributes Star Coins — representing medicine — to swallows representing the sick and wounded, forming a "dialectic of giving and receiving": Claudia's symmetrical balanced posture and even distribution of Star Coins symbolize precise measurement of resource allocation; the downward scattering of coins corresponds to the orderly flow of material wealth; the swallows spreading their wings to receive the coins form a vivid miniature of social stratification; Claudia's neat, elegant robes against the humble swallows reinforce the stark contrast of the material world; mountain walls in the background hint at stable social structures. When wealth and power reach a certain equilibrium, generosity is both the fulfillment of social responsibility and the manifestation of cosmic law.

At the center of the card stands the 麥穗 — Seven of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 855 of the Circular Calendar, agronomist Livia discovered through seven years of experiments that high-purity Ash Matter had a remarkable catalytic effect on northern wild rye. Lower purity had been more stable early on, but by year four the pure-substance test field's yield doubled versus the control and gained disease resistance; the full ears that formed took the shape of Star Coins — confirming the enormous agricultural application potential of high-purity Ash Matter. In the image agronomist Livia stands in contemplation facing the grain, gazing at the seven Star Coin-shaped ears on the stalk. Seven Star Coins hanging from a vine symbolize the fruits of labor at an intermediate stage. Livia's contemplative posture, leaning on the stalk, corresponds to the weighing of current harvest against future strategy. The tilled field at her feet represents effort already invested and a foundation already laid. Five living leaves on the vine hint at potential still growing. The unfinished fence behind her echoes the protective system still needing completion. The farmhouse faintly visible in the distance reminds of the ultimate material home and long-term goal. When initial effort has been converted into visible results, a momentary pause and deep thinking outweigh blind action.

At the center of the card stands the 石音 — Eight of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. Star Coin carver Cecilia showed exceptional talent from childhood. In year 879 of the Circular Calendar she discovered that striking and grinding Star Stones at specific frequencies could optimize the internal distribution of Ash Matter, significantly improving their resonance efficiency with miracle circuits. Though she trained five apprentices, no one could match her core intuitive technique of "listening to the stone's voice." In her later years she wrote Standard Procedures for Star Stone Processing, which became the official protocol; her personal notebooks, rich with intuitive descriptions, were designated as reference material. In the image the focused craftsperson Cecilia carefully carves and listens to the final Star Coin in her workshop. Seven finished Star Coins arranged neatly together with the eighth half-finished piece being worked above form a complete cycle of quantitative change leading to qualitative change. Cecilia's focused hands and balanced posture reflect total dedication of self to professional skill. The ring-shaped equipment behind her symbolizes a systematic workflow. Star-light patterns in the background environment suggest the connection between the fruits of labor and social value. A moon crown gleaming with light at her head, combined with her simple garment, presents the perfect union of passion and wisdom. The large white straight wings behind her allude to the sacred process of transforming fundamental action into artistic creation.

At the center of the card stands the Lady of Lichen — Nine of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 908 of the Circular Calendar, researcher Isabel cultivated a lichen capable of absorbing ambient Ash Matter, forming a natural counter-surveillance barrier and achieving energy self-circulation. By 912, the third-generation Ash Matter lichen was promoted nationally by the church — it could adhere to Ash Matter in the air and form a dynamic protective layer. The church erected an arc-shaped sculpture in the Wilderness Valley to commemorate her. In the image the elegantly dressed Lady of Lichen Isabel stands on a wilderness stone bridge covered in lichen, gently stroking a falcon. The obedient falcon resting at her fingertip symbolizes tamed wild power and precise mastery. Her right hand raised slightly in front of her body speaks of treasuring and protecting the fruits of labor. The special lichen she cultivated clusters and spreads at her feet, singing praise to this self-satisfied Lady of Lichen. Nine Star Coins revolving in the great arc-shaped sculpture behind her form a massive spiritual symbol. The stone platforms and bridges connecting below represent a carefully planned life territory. Her plain white long robe and streamlined decorations embody the fusion of abundance and wisdom. Distant grey stars hint at a solid spiritual foundation.

At the center of the card stands the 采星 — Ten of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 950 of the Circular Calendar, the family of elder sister Margria (White Triangle) and younger sister Margrit (White Triangle) was granted permanent use-rights to a Star Coin because five consecutive generations had managed the Star Stone mining records for the church. Under their supervision the family compiled the Star Vein Genealogy — recording in detail the discovery of major veins, their extraction decline curves, and predicted reserves. This book became the foundational document for strategic planning, ensuring stable inheritance and management of Star Stone resources within the family system. In the image family members Margria and Margrit stand respectively beneath symmetrical archways. The passageway threaded with musical-note-like silk cords symbolizes the eternal continuation of guarding a family enterprise. The sisters' specially-made family hats correspond to the spiritual core of lineage. The gesture of both leaning forward to lightly stroke the silk cords alludes to the intergenerational transmission of values. The two sisters beneath the arch, balanced and symmetrical, represent different stages of family vitality. The ten Star Coins hanging in the arch announce the completeness of material achievement like a triumphal arch. The great spiritual sphere in the latticework background echoes the law of order in the material world.

At the center of the card stands the 提純 — Page of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 783 of the Circular Calendar, apprentice Grete was assigned to record a Star Coin preparation process. She was not permitted to operate, but observed that when her teacher filtered Ash Matter impurities, the surface temperature of the container holding the impurities dropped instantaneously. She privately compared 37 preparation records and found a positive correlation between the magnitude of temperature decrease and the final purity of the Ash Matter. She wrote her discovery into a preliminary report that was not immediately adopted, but the data was later included in the Yearbook of Ash Matter Purification Phenomenon Observations. In the image young Grete reverently holds a Star Coin aloft with both hands, standing in vast open fields of a spiritual sea. The focused posture of carefully holding the coin symbolizes precious thirst for knowledge and skill. The coin's glimmer in sunlight corresponds to the continuous manifestation of latent value. The undulating field at her feet represents fertile growth territory yet to be cultivated. Wings curling into a rectangular archway-like structure embody the steadiness of the earth element. Birds fluttering freely around the coin echo the surge of newly born energy. Her focused gaze on the coin shows the rigor of systematic learning. The yearning posture of leaning forward hints at deep observation before internalizing knowledge.

At the center of the card stands the 越穹 — Knight of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In the Triangle Church's "Star Crossing" ceremony, knight Berenice prepared with extreme practicality for three months, precisely calculating the path and weight distribution. During the competition she maintained a steady pace — especially at the fifth corridor's turning point, where she used anticipation and centrifugal control to accelerate smoothly, with no wasted motion throughout. In the end she not only won the championship and broke the record but became the only champion in a decade to maintain a steady speed for the entire course, earning the Star Coin of honor. In the image the steady knight Berenice sits upright on a sure-footed black deer. The Star Coin she holds with one hand symbolizes focused protection of material value. The black deer's firm tread on the celestial path corresponds to the measured pace of steady accumulation. Her smooth, solid garments represent a complete self-protection system. The flowing cape trailing behind hides undiminished enthusiasm for action. The figure's unhurried, controlled posture reveals a composed mastery. The firm foundation where the celestial path meets the earth hints at a career grounded in solid reality. The brilliant radiance in the distance forms a life pattern of sustainable development, reflecting precious values refined by time.

At the center of the card stands the 星語 — Queen of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 845 of the Circular Calendar, Black Triangle Eloise presided over the expansion of the Star Language Library. She secured a larger Star Coin budget for acquiring documents and researching the activation of miracles, and established a system of document authentication and restoration based on Star Coin energy resonance. She strongly supported opening non-classified knowledge to vetted lower-ranking members, believing that "the circulation of knowledge is itself a form of nourishment." Under her tenure, the library's collection and utilization rate both increased dramatically. In 865, to commemorate her outstanding contributions, the church cast a statue tens of meters tall in her honor — it still stands today in the northeast corner of church headquarters. In the image the self-satisfied Black Triangle Eloise stands atop the great sculpture, gazing down from the highest point at the Star Language Library she oversaw. White swallows flying beside the sculpture symbolize the abundant gifts of natural cycles. The great Star Coin glimmering beside it radiates steady luster like scrutinizing the crystallization of life. The sharp crown at the head of the sculpture and the smooth flowing lines below form a perfect balance of passion and gentleness. The complex interwoven spiritual-world threads in the background construct her pragmatic, abundant inner world.

At the center of the card stands the 法典 — King of Pentacles of the Yizhu Grey Listener world. In year 607 of the Circular Calendar, resource coordination minister Violeta promulgated the Code of Star Coin Management and Use, unifying casting standards and approval procedures, and establishing an audit mechanism to trace fifty years of usage records — acting on this to discipline three members in violation. This move established order with an iron hand, bringing Star Coin resources firmly under church control and laying a solid foundation for its development over the next hundred years. In the image the imposing administrative coordinator Violeta stands on an elaborately carved stone platform, on the eve of the promulgation of the Code of Star Coin Management and Use she planned — repeatedly deliberating the details of its provisions to better perfect the system. The mountain ranges on either side of the platform symbolize the steady force of the earth element and the foundation of worldly achievement. The solid base behind her corresponds to the material empire precisely planned. The Star Coin scepter beside her forms a dual symbol of wealth accumulation and natural force. The flowing star rail at her feet proclaims absolute mastery of material laws. Bird-wing-shaped head armor alludes to the symbiosis of abundance and success. A flickering star crown hovering above hints at the ultimate authority to unlock the mysteries of the material world. When experience, capital, and will are refined in the furnace of reality, every decision will be transformed into transmissible eternal value.
